children: The Reserve Bank of India likely intervened in the foreign exchange market on Tuesday, four traders told Reuters, as rising oil prices and growing wagers on a rate hike in the U.S. this week pressured the South Asian unit.
declined 0.2% to 95.79 per dollar, hovering around its weakest levels in a month.
State-run banks were spotted offering dollars, most likely on behalf of the RBI, the traders said.
The dollar sales were not "especially heavy" in nature and were likely intended to limit excessive volatility, a trader at a Mumbai-based bank said.
was last up 1.2% at $106.9 per barrel.
The central bank was also likely conducting dollar-rupee sell/buy swaps, traders said, marking the fourth straight session in which the RBI has used swaps to drain excess rupee liquidity.
Dollar-rupee forward premiums were a tad higher, with the August 2027 month-end premium ticking up 2 paisa to 3.07 rupees.
